title: Over-permissioned read_file: path traversal reads files outside the workspace
summary: Arbitrary file disclosure to the model context, and from there to the user or to an exfiltration channel.

LC.rationale: In the default CLI a user request is natural language that the model turns into a read_file call, and the harness runs that call with no independent reduction of the path to a closed, validated field. The writeup also names injection, but a confused request is an unmediated direct path.

CP.rationale: The documented steps and the in-repo proof are a single read_file call that returns source file contents; they do not write the long-term memory file or show attacker context surviving the session.

AP.rationale: The file contents are returned to the same office-assistant model under one identity, and the lab states multi-agent handoffs are out of scope, so intent does not cross into another agent, tenant, or policy domain.

RH.rationale: The S2 materials show path traversal via a direct tool call and do not describe an evaluator, verifier, reward channel, or a verified episode of satisfying a proxy by crossing a security boundary, nor a test that those channels are isolated.

ES.rationale: By default all twelve built-in tools are offered and arguments are not validated; read_file joins the supplied path with no containment check, so the callable argument is not independently constrained on this path.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the office assistant as a model-directed loop that selects and sequences tool calls; scripted worst-case models are the test stand-in, even though the S2 proof invokes the tool directly.
